content.title: Clockwork Typography Variant | Gear Duties, Disorder and Reset
content.summary: Establish one clearly adult original subject and a clockwork coordinate system before text moves. Require one visible subject action before each exact word engages a mechanical duty. Assign each word one distinct pendulum, gear, spring, rewind or loop behavior. Escalate mechanical scale or disorder while preserving subject identity and the same coordinate system. Return every mechanism to a readable zero state around the same adult identity anchor.

quick_start.input_format: Establish one clearly adult original subject and a clockwork coordinate system before text moves. + Require one visible subject action before each exact word engages a mechanical duty. + Assign each word one distinct pendulum, gear, spring, rewind or loop behavior. + Escalate mechanical scale or disorder while preserving subject identity and the same coordinate system. + Return every mechanism to a readable zero state around the same adult identity anchor.
quick_start.recommended_input: In an original copper-and-teal theater fly tower, establish one clearly adult stage technician in a charcoal jumpsuit inside a fixed rigging grid; preserve face, shaved hair and center line. She turns a handwheel and the exact word 'LIFT' becomes meshed gears; she releases a spring and the exact word 'TURN' coils around one pulley, one duty per word. She presses one red reset button; all cables return to their marks and the exact final word 'HOME' locks around the same adult portrait at mechanical zero.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one clearly adult original subject and a clockwork coordinate system before text moves. Require one visible subject action before each exact word engages a mechanical duty. Assign each word one distinct pendulum, gear, spring, rewind or loop behavior. Escalate mechanical scale or disorder while preserving subject identity and the same coordinate system. Return every mechanism to a readable zero state around the same adult identity anchor. The reusable mechanism is the ordered baseline, trigger, continuity, controlled escalation and terminal proof—not the source identities, brands, wording, locations, props, exact styling, choreography, camera path, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one clearly adult original subject and a clockwork coordinate system before text moves.
invariants.purpose: Makes the baseline measurable before the mechanism changes it.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without the baseline, later change has no trustworthy reference state.

invariants.rule: Require one visible subject action before each exact word engages a mechanical duty.
invariants.purpose: Binds the first visible change to a specific cause rather than decoration.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a visible trigger, the transition reads as an arbitrary edit.

invariants.rule: Assign each word one distinct pendulum, gear, spring, rewind or loop behavior.
invariants.purpose: Preserves identity, material or spatial continuity through the middle transition.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without continuity, the sequence becomes unrelated montage or identity drift.

invariants.rule: Escalate mechanical scale or disorder while preserving subject identity and the same coordinate system.
invariants.purpose: Raises intensity or information while retaining the same readable grammar.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without controlled escalation, the middle either plateaus or turns into noise.

invariants.rule: Return every mechanism to a readable zero state around the same adult identity anchor.
invariants.purpose: Provides a terminal proof that resolves the mechanism instead of merely stopping.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without terminal proof, the promised result or reversal remains unverified.
